newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury deliberates on punitive damages.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury deliberates on punitive damages.

text.p: Jurors in O.J. Simpson's civil trial Monday started their second day of deliberations on whether the former football star should pay punitive damages for the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

The panel last Tuesday blamed Simpson for the June 1994 murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman and awarded Goldman's divorced parents $8.5 million in compensatory damages. The lawsuit filed by Nicole Brown Simpson's estate did not seek such damages but would share in any punitive damages.

The jury last week heard widely conflicting accounts of Simpson's financial status. His lawyers claimed he was in debt to the tune of more than $9 million, including the $8.5 damages awarded against him, while lawyers for the plaintiffs sought to show that Simpson had a net worth of more than $15 million and could earn $2 million to $3 million a year with product endorsements and autograph signings.
Simpson was acquitted of the murders by a criminal court jury in October 1995 but was sued by the families of the victims for wrongful death.
